title: Working Out the Machines One Collection Run Carries on Renew Business Asset Buyback
content:
**The figure.** The units one collection may carry are the machines the agreement covers, capped at the full batch allowance the carrier books for a collection on the programme, and the run lifts those machines in full. The figure the customer consents to is a whole count of machines. The full batch allowance the carrier books for a collection on a Renew Business Asset Buyback agreement is 40 machines, and the whole share a run lifts is 100 per cent of what it is left with.

**Where the machines come from.** The machines the agreement covers are the devices standing on the Renew Business Asset Buyback agreement itself, taken as the count of devices that agreement records.

**The order the figure is reached in.** The units one collection may carry are worked out in one order and no other. The machines the agreement covers are first capped at the batch allowance the carrier books. The machines held back for a claim and the machines held back while a service crew is attending are then taken off that capped figure, leaving never fewer than none. The share the run lifts is applied last to what that step leaves, that share being taken of it, and the result is rounded down to a whole machine.

**Worked figure on hypothetical inputs.** Take a Renew Business Asset Buyback agreement covering 57 machines.

1. The machines the agreement covers, 57, are capped at the batch allowance of 40 machines, giving 40.
2. Nothing is taken off that figure, so 40 machines stand.
3. The whole share of 100 per cent is applied to 40, giving 40, and 40 is already a whole machine.

The units one collection may carry are therefore 40 machines. Take instead an agreement covering 22 machines: the cap of 40 does not bite, 22 machines stand, the whole share of 100 per cent leaves 22, and the units one collection may carry are 22 machines.

**Rounding.** The figure is rounded down to a whole machine, so a share that leaves a part machine gives the whole machine below it and never the one above.
